Sanjay (Product Designer): quick design check — sketch for a 'staged approval lanes' flow for prompt-sets + scorecards. idea: reviewers can move runs across lanes (needs review, accept, flag, follow-up) and we show a confidence badge per run. mock: https://redwood.mock/s/staged-lanes :eyes: Michelle (PM): digging this. main questions: how does bulk-approve behave across lanes? and what's the CTA copy for 'move to follow-up'? Sanjay (Product Designer): bulk will open a small modal with lane pick and an optional note. CTA copy proposals: 'Move to follow-up (add note)' or 'Bulk move to follow-up'. open to wordsmithing. Ada (Frontend Eng): implementation note — moving runs may interact badly with keyboard focus and screenreader announcements. If modal appears we need focus trap and an aria-live update when the move completes. Also batch ops must respect rate limits from eval-run-api. Frank (Accessibility): +1 on aria-live. For seamless SR experience use: ``
Moved 12 runs to Follow-up
``. Also ensure lane headers are real landmarks so screenreader users can jump between lanes. Contrast of lane chips: current mock fails AA on 14px. Eva (Research): one more UX datapoint — reviewers often want to see the failing example inline when moving to Follow-up. Can we surface the top failing sample as a collapsed preview in the modal? helps triage. Michelle (PM): love the collapsed preview idea. Also thinking about 'confidence badges' — should they be algorithmic (eval model confidence) or worker-supplied? maybe both: a small AI badge + optional manual override. copy: 'AI confidence: 87% — override' Sanjay (Product Designer): new wire: small badge with tooltip, clicking allows quick override and a reason. We probably need an audit log entry when overridden. Ada (Frontend Eng): audit log is fine. Need API shape: suggestion: ``POST /runs/bulk_move {\"run_ids\": [...], \"target_lane\": \"follow_up\", \"note\": \"...\", \"overrides\": [{\"id\": \"run-1\",\"confidence_override\":\"low\"}]}`` — this will let backend persist overrides. keep payload small. Frank (Accessibility): quick a11y nit — keyboard users hitting the lane toggle can't see the tooltip on hover. tooltips need an accessible trigger (focusable element) and a visible focus ring. Also add aria-describedby linking to the tooltip content. Sanjay (Product Designer): noted. I'll update the mock: make badge a button with title and an optional inline label. Michelle (PM): one more product constraint — approvals need a 'revert' option for 24 hours after bulk approve, and we should surface an undo snackbar with 'Undo' action. Accessibility: snackbar should be in role=\"alert\" so SR picks it up. Frank (Accessibility): alert role is ok for immediate ephemeral updates. For undo we must ensure keyboard focus returns to the last focused run after undo completes. Eva (Research): can we add a tiny 'regression diff peek' in the scorecard — a +/- emblem that expands a short diff snippet without leaving the page? testers said context loss kills speed. Ada (Frontend Eng): feasible — render a small inline diff with aria-hidden on purely visual bits; but the diff must be keyboard-expandable. Also add a 'copy example' button for quick repro. Sanjay (Product Designer): will wire that. final asks before I ship updated mock: (1) exact CTA wording for bulk move, (2) undo UX acceptance window (24h?), (3) accessibility checklist items. Michelle (PM): (1) 'Move to Follow-up' (2) 24h is fine (3) checklist: focus trap on modal, aria-live status for moves, role=alert for snackbar, lane headers as landmarks, tooltips accessible. I'll coordinate with legal for audit retention. Ada (Frontend Eng): leaving a note about rate limits and optimistic UI: let's show a progress row per run during bulk moves and only show final snackbar when all finished. prevents partial confusion. Sanjay (Product Designer): perfect. I'll push a new figma and drop it here. tagging @redwood-bot to post updated asset. redwood-bot: Design asset uploaded: https://redwood.mock/s/staged-lanes/v2 — file id 3b9f. Michelle (PM): thanks folks — follow-up sync 1pm tomorrow if needed. :calendar:
